jsonld.name: Student Loan Calculator
jsonld.description: Calculate your monthly student or school loan payment, total interest, and payoff date. Works for federal and private loans. Free, instant, no signup.

mainEntity.name: Does this model income-driven repayment plans?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, in simplified form: it estimates Income-Based Repayment (IBR) at 10% of income above 150% of the poverty guideline, capped at the standard 10-year payment, holding your income constant. Real IDR payments are recalculated every year, so your actual payment and total cost can differ.

mainEntity.name: Should I pay off student loans early?

acceptedAnswer.text: This depends on your interest rate relative to other financial priorities — paying extra toward high-rate loans generally makes sense, though some borrowers prioritize building emergency savings or capturing employer retirement matches first.

mainEntity.name: What is loan forgiveness and am I eligible?

acceptedAnswer.text: Various federal forgiveness programs exist for specific careers (like public service) or after extended income-driven repayment — eligibility rules are specific and change periodically, so check current federal guidance directly.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between federal and private student loans?

acceptedAnswer.text: Federal loans typically offer more borrower protections, flexible repayment plans, and potential forgiveness programs, while private loans are based on creditworthiness and generally offer less flexibility but sometimes lower rates for well-qualified borrowers.

mainEntity.name: How do I calculate my student loan monthly payment?

acceptedAnswer.text: Use the standard amortization formula: M = P[r(1+r)^n]/[(1+r)^n-1], where P is principal, r is monthly interest rate (annual rate ÷ 12), and n is number of payments. Enter your loan details above for an instant result.

mainEntity.name: What is the average student loan monthly payment?

acceptedAnswer.text: The average monthly student loan payment for a 10-year standard repayment plan on a $30,000 federal student loan at 6.5% is approximately $340/month. Use this calculator to find your specific payment.

mainEntity.name: How much is a $50,000 student loan monthly payment?

acceptedAnswer.text: A $50,000 student loan at 6.5% over 10 years has a monthly payment of approximately $567/month, with total interest of about $18,000 over the life of the loan.

mainEntity.name: What will my student loan monthly payment be?

acceptedAnswer.text: Your monthly student loan payment depends on three things: the loan amount, interest rate, and repayment term. For example, a $30,000 loan at 6.5% over 10 years has a monthly payment of about $340. Use this calculator to enter your specific figures and get an exact amount.

mainEntity.name: How do I estimate my student loan payments before taking out a loan?

acceptedAnswer.text: Enter the expected loan amount, the interest rate offered, and your preferred repayment term (10 years is standard for federal loans). This calculator shows your monthly payment, total interest paid, and total cost — so you can compare different loan amounts before committing.
